Calculate leaf wetness duration (wet-hours) from relative humidity and rainfall

Source: R/leaf_wetness.R
dot-calculate_leaf_wetness.Rd

Calculates daily leaf wetness duration as wet-hours from 0 to 24 using relative humidity and rainfall. The wet-hours output can then be mapped to an infection-rate multiplier from 0 to 1 using an RcW curve (hours -> 0 to 1).

Usage

.calculate_leaf_wetness(wth, rhlim, rainlim, weighted_wetness = FALSE)

Arguments

wth

Weather data in the proper format.

rhlim

Relative humidity threshold (%) used to determine wetness.

rainlim

Rainfall scaling threshold (mm per wet-hour equivalent).

weighted_wetness

If TRUE, compute weighted hourly wetness (0 to 24); if FALSE, count hours where hourly RH >= rhlim (0 to 24).

Value

A numeric vector of daily wet-hours from 0 to 24, length nrow(wth). Use with RcW (hours -> 0 to 1) to obtain the wetness multiplier for infection.

Details

Two modes are supported:

  • Unweighted (default): counts the number of hourly RH values >= rhlim (0 to 24 wet-hours).

  • Weighted (weighted_wetness = TRUE): converts each hourly RH value to a wetness weight from 0 to 1 (0 below 80%, 1 at/above rhlim) and sums weights across 24 hours (0 to 24 wet-hours).

Rainfall contributes additional wet-hours proportional to RAIN / rainlim, capped at 24, and combined without double-counting by scaling to the remaining dry fraction of the day. If TMIN/TMAX are missing, the function falls back to a binary wetness day (0 or 24 wet-hours) based on rhlim/rainlim thresholds.

Author

Adam H. Sparks, adamhsparks@gmail.com

Examples

wth <- get_wth(
  lonlat = c(121.25562, 14.6774),
  dates = c("2000-06-30", "2000-07-31")
)

wet_simple <- .calculate_leaf_wetness(
  wth = wth,
  rhlim = 90,
  rainlim = 5,
  weighted_wetness = FALSE
)
#> Error in .calculate_leaf_wetness(wth = wth, rhlim = 90, rainlim = 5, weighted_wetness = FALSE): could not find function ".calculate_leaf_wetness"
summary(wet_simple)
#> Error: object 'wet_simple' not found
